round_defaults.query: Run exactly one patrol pass against the current alert queue. First call alert.fetch. Review enough evidence to explain the active intrusion. Keep this round budget-aware: target <=12 tool calls, avoid one-call-per-alert fan-out for homogeneous alerts, and reserve turns for final output. If current alerts justify a new case or the referenced case record does not exist yet, call alert.detail-batch with at least one representative alert first, then create or refresh the case with case.upsert-batch using the exact case.upsert-batch schema keys from the MCP prompt only (single-case writes also use one-item batch). Do not send extra case.upsert-batch fields such as description, severity, created_at, or updated_at. Then use case tools to maintain case state when justified, always include numeric confidence and reason in each case.link-alert-batch item, call case.update-risk to persist a case-level assessment snapshot whenever this run advances stage, raises severity, or forms a new case-level judgment even if the case header is already synced, persist entity-level conclusions with the exact assessment.upsert-batch schema keys from the MCP prompt, include compromised_host for an asset when exploitation/webshell/foothold evidence supports it, and ack any alert you have triaged in one batch call whenever possible. When linking alerts/entities/actor-relations in one pass, prefer case.link-alert-batch, assessment.upsert-batch, actor.case-link-batch, and actor.case-add-observation-batch. For same-stage events in one case, prefer one aggregated timeline.upsert node instead of per-alert timeline fan-out. Output the final answer with these Markdown headers exactly: '## Patrol Action Summary', '## Remaining Uncertainty', '## Memory Summary'.
